title.narrative: Second Bridges Improvement and Maintenance Program

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Bridges Improvement and Maintenance Program for Nepal is to provide safe, resilient, and cost-effective bridges on Nepal's Strategic Roads Network. The proposed operation is designed as a ‘hybrid’ operation, which includes both Program-for-Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF) components.Developing and/or maintaining bridge infrastructure in the Strategic Roads Network under the Bridge Branch, as set forth in the Bridge Policy and Strategy, including: (a) providing road safety upgrades on existing bridges; (b) constructing new bridges; (c) completing bridges under construction; (d) major bridge maintenance; and (e) carrying out bridge designs, site assessments, feasibility studies, quality monitoring,environmental and social impact management, and providing logistics support, for the Program, as required for the preparation and supervision of civil works.This IPF Component: Consultancy Support and Institutional Development will support the following: (a) provision of consultancy support and institutional development to the Recipient to prepare Potential Future Projects within the Strategic Roads Network, such as, including but not limited to, preparation of baseline assessments, engineering studies, feasibility studies, safeguard assessments and technical designs; (b) carrying out technical audits through the National Vigilance Center, identifying instances where implementation of works deviates from expected technical and process-related standards or specifications; (c) developing advanced bridge designs to: (i) enhance resilience to extreme weather or seismic events; and (ii) include pedestrians and cyclists access; (d) Provision of Training to develop the DOR staff and other stakeholders technical, social, environmental and fiduciary capabilities; (e) strengthening the institutional capacity of the Bridge Branch for the carrying out of supervision and oversight activities on the Strategic Roads Network under the Operation; (f) mobilizing, equipping and developing the Design and Advanced Technology Cell; (g) improving DOR's occupational and community health and safety practices and its capacity to implement the Labor Act; (h) verification activities support. (i) collecting data for the impact evaluation of the Program.
To provide safe, resilient and cost effective bridges on Nepal's Strategic Road Network.

title.narrative: Anticipated beneficiaries of inclusive design concepts

comment.narrative:
More than 1,000 people are expected to benefit from the inclusive design concept of the two advance bridges namely, Narayani and Bijayapur bridges.
Further, the expected beneficiaries are disaggregated as: (i) Bijayapur bridge: 22,850 male; 25,488 female; 1,969 vulnerable individuals (ii) Narayani Bridge:13,362 male and 13,986 female; 1,826 vulnerable individuals.
This original target was revised twice: (i) second restructuring reduced to 2,000 number (ii) third restructuring reduced to 1,000 number.
(Source: Environment and Social Screening Report based on CBS 2021 data of Narayani and Bijayapur Bridges, June 2024)

title.narrative: Number of times that DoR engineers mobilized skills in the designing of advanced bridges for improved resilience and inclusion.

comment.narrative:
The Program conducted two (2) number of workshops during the design of two advanced bridges under the DATC.
The indicator definition was revised during the first restructuring as: Number of workshops completed by DoR on the design of advanced bridges for improved resilience and inclusion (ex. consultancies/ DATC training).
(Source: Borrower's ICR report, August 2024)

title.narrative: Construction of New Bridges to reduce road user costs

comment.narrative:
The Program exceeded the target by construction of 4,426.65 (52 number) new bridges.
The original target was increased to 4,400 meters through first restructuring.
(Source: Borrower's ICR Report, August 2024)

title.narrative: Implementation of high priority maintenance to extend asset lives

comment.narrative:
The Program exceeded the target by implementation of major maintenance in 5,839 meters (59 number) of bridges.
The original target was revised twice: (i) second restructuring increased to 5,000 meters; and (ii) third restructuring increased to 5,700 meters.
(Source: Borrower's ICR, August 2024)

title.narrative: Road Safety upgrades on Progam Bridges

comment.narrative:
The Program exceeded the target by upgrading road safety features on 8,118 meters bridges.
(Source: Borrower's ICR report, August 2024)

title.narrative: Completion of backlog bridges to reduce road user costs

comment.narrative:
The Program exceeded the target by completion of 8,660 meters (90 numbers) backlog bridges.
The original target was revised thrice : (i) first restructuring increased to 6,500 meters (ii) second restructuring increased to 7,300 meters (iii) third restructuring increased to 8,565 meters.
(Source: Borrower's ICR, August 2024)

title.narrative: Responsiveness to bridges related complaints through the DOR's Grievance Redress Mechanism

comment.narrative:
The Program reported resolving of total 24 number of bridge related grievances in an average of 9 days within the Program period.
(Source: Borrower's ICR report, August 2024)

title.narrative: Female Engineers recruited in the Design and Advanced Technology Cell and given advanced skills training

comment.narrative:
The Program recruited >33% of female engineers in the DATC and provided them with the advance skills trainings.
Out of total 18 engineers recruited, 7 female engineers composed of 2 SDEs, 4 engineers, and 1 consultant.
Source: (Fifth ISR AM; and Borrower's ICR report, August 2024

title.narrative: Design and Advanced Technology Cell created

comment.narrative:
The DATC was established/equipped with 18 numbers of members trained and mobilized.
(Source: Fifth ISR AM; and Borrower's ICR report, August, 2024)

actual.value: The DATC cell has been created, staffed and mobilized as per the approved ToR and notified through DoR letter dated July 13, 2021.

title.narrative: Reduced likelihood of road departure crashes on Program Bridges

comment.narrative:
The Program exceeded the target by upgrading road safety visual signs on around 100 number (6,565 meters) of bridges.
(Source: Borrower's ICR, August 2024)

title.narrative: Enhanced DOR capabilites for developing resilient bridge designs

comment.narrative:
The Program developed two (2) new bridge design concepts for Narayani and Bijaypur bridges under the DATC, incorporating advanced features for enhanced resilience and inclusion.
The original target was revised twice: (i) second restructuring reduced to 4 number (ii) third restructuring reduced to 2 number.
(Source: Borrower's ICR, August 2024)
